## Why

Looking at data is most of what you did in RStudio's Environment pane and viewer, and most of what you added extensions for in VS Code. Positron builds it in: Variables, Data Explorer, Plots, and Help.

If these four panes feel natural, most of your daily work has moved.

## What you will have at the end

- Your lab's data inspected without writing inspection code
- One Data Explorer step kept as code
- Plots from both languages found, traced to their source, and saved
- Help found without leaving Positron

**Time box:** 40 minutes on top of your lab. The R half is capped at 20.

## How to work this file

- Each task states an outcome. Finding the how is part of the check.
- Where a task asks you to predict, write the prediction before you test it.
- The hint names the Positron docs page to read if you get stuck. Use it only after trying.

## Checks

- [ ] I can open a data frame in the Data Explorer from the Variables pane, the editor, and the Console
- [ ] I found missing values and a distribution without writing code
- [ ] I turned a Data Explorer step into code
- [ ] I can move through plot history and get from a plot to its code
- [ ] I can open help for a function inside Positron
- [ ] I did the R half in 20 minutes or less
